fluff.overview: The Svartalfa is a fourteen-ton ultraheavy ProtoMek developed by Clan Hell's Horses, representing a radical leap in ProtoMek design philosophy. Initially mistaken for a light or ultralight LAM by intelligence analysts due to its flight capability, the Svartalfa is in fact an enormous ProtoMek equipped with a wing-in-ground effect gliding system that allows limited low-altitude flight at speeds exceeding sixty kilometers per hour. At half again the mass of any previously known ProtoMek, the Svartalfa mounts more armor than most twenty-ton BattleMeks and carries a weapons suite that can challenge medium Meks in direct combat. The design's existence was first revealed when Clan Wolf became an unwitting live-fire test subject, and the Wolves struggled to understand what they were facing: too small to be a Mek, but far too tough to be battle armor or any known ProtoMek.
fluff.capabilities:
The Svartalfa's most distinctive feature is its wing-in-ground effect gliding system. While incapable of true flight or transformation like a Land-Air Mek, the Svartalfa uses deployable wings to glide just above the ground surface at cruising speeds of forty-three kilometers per hour, with a flank speed approaching sixty-five. On foot, the massive ProtoMek moves at a crawl barely exceeding ten kilometers per hour, making the gliding mode essential for tactical maneuvering. The wings fold compactly for ground operations and transport, and their robust construction allows them to absorb weapons fire without significantly degrading gliding performance.

The Svartalfa's weapons suite punches well above its weight class. Twin arm-mounted Medium Chemical Lasers deliver damage comparable to Inner Sphere medium lasers without requiring the heat dissipation systems that standard energy weapons demand, though their chemical fuel supply limits operational endurance to approximately thirty salvos total. A Streak SRM-6 launcher in the main gun mount provides devastating close-range firepower with ten guided salvos, while a torso-mounted machine gun with fifty rounds handles anti-infantry work. Sixty-four points of armor can survive a heavy Gauss rifle hit to the torso at point-blank range, making the Svartalfa extraordinarily resilient for any combat unit below twenty tons. The cockpit is fifty percent larger than standard ProtoMek designs, allowing pilots of Elemental phenotype to operate the machine, though it can be reconfigured for smaller pilots as well.
fluff.deployment: The base Svartalfa mounts twin arm-mounted Medium Chemical Lasers with fifteen rounds each, a Streak SRM-6 launcher in the main gun position with ten guided salvos, and a torso-mounted machine gun with fifty rounds of ammunition. The wing-in-ground effect system provides gliding movement at forty-three kilometers per hour cruising speed, while ground speed is limited to approximately ten kilometers per hour. Sixty-four points of armor make the base Svartalfa extraordinarily durable, capable of absorbing punishment that would destroy most light Meks. The enlarged cockpit accommodates pilots of Elemental phenotype. Produced at Swedenborg Heavy Industries on Kirchbach, the Svartalfa is distributed exclusively to the Hell's Horses' best ProtoMek pilots in elite formations.
fluff.history:
Intelligence gathered from Diamond Shark trade delegations first hinted at the Svartalfa's existence through rumors of Clan Hell's Horses developing a light or ultralight LAM. One distant image was obtained showing a flying object, but covert missions to ferret out more information all ended in failure. The truth was revealed when the Horses deployed the Svartalfa against Clan Wolf in live combat, leaving the Wolves thoroughly confused about what they faced. Too small for a Mek but far too durable for any known battle armor or ProtoMek, the Svartalfa took considerable time and casualties before Wolf warriors learned to counter it effectively.

The Svartalfa has been distributed exclusively to the Hell's Horses' best ProtoMek pilots in elite units. In raids against the Wolves, the design proved its worth both in direct combat and in the confusion it sowed. Deploying medium and heavy Meks to engage even a single ProtoMek frustrated Wolf MekWarriors, while attempts to counter with battle armor failed due to the Svartalfa's decisive advantages in armor, firepower, and mobility. The design provides a low-resource unit that can tie down far more complex opponents, freeing heavier forces to concentrate on fewer targets.

A dedicated fire support variant, the Svartalfa 2, was developed by Hell's Horses scientists who managed to mount dual fifteen-tube long-range missile racks, one in the torso and one as a main gun. This required significant armor reduction but provided devastating long-range barrage capability. A Point of LRM-equipped Svartalfas with a forward spotter once convinced a Star of Wolf Meks that they were engaging a Bane hiding in the woods, rotating the spotter position to keep the Wolves guessing while ravaging them with indirect fire. The Svartalfa 3 takes a different approach, mounting five Medium Chemical Lasers for sustained energy-weapon engagements at the cost of the Streak launcher and machine gun.
